faq: Which feed formats can you create?
CSV, XML and the marketplace templates, including Amazon inventory files, Google Merchant Center feeds and eBay file exchange. We choose the format that your platform and marketplace support best.
Can the feed update stock and prices on its own?
Yes, in Standard and Premium, where the store platform or a feed app allows it. Some marketplaces limit how often they read a feed. We set the schedule within those limits.
Do I need a feed app, and does it cost money?
Sometimes. Where a free route exists we use it. If a paid feed app is clearly better, we show the monthly price and the free option so you can choose. The app is billed to you directly.
What if the marketplace rejects products in the feed?
We read the error report and fix the data causes, such as missing barcodes or wrong categories. Rejections that come from the marketplace's own policy review stay the marketplace's decision.
desc:
Product data feed setup for marketplaces gives Amazon, Google and other channels a clean, structured file of your catalog. Ecom Swift LLC cleans your data, maps each field and tests the feed with the marketplace's own checker.

## What is a product data feed?

A product data feed is a file or live connection that lists your products with the fields a marketplace needs: title, description, price, stock, images, identifiers, category and shipping details. It is usually a spreadsheet, a text file or an XML file, and it can refresh on a schedule. Marketplaces and shopping channels read it to build or update your listings.

Every channel names its fields a little differently and has its own required values. A feed is the translation layer between your store and each one.

## Why messy data causes trouble

Products with missing barcodes, wrong categories or unusual formatting are rejected, or they appear with mistakes. A price that does not match your store can lead to disapproved items. Stock that does not update can lead to orders you cannot fill.

Cleaning data once, at the source, is much cheaper than fixing the same errors on every channel. Duplicate titles, mixed units and inconsistent brand names are usually easy to correct in bulk.

## How a good feed affects results

A clean feed gets more of your catalog accepted and keeps it accurate. Accepted products can be shown to shoppers, so the feed determines how much of your range is visible at all. Correct titles and attributes help channels match products to search queries.

We cannot promise that a channel will accept every item or how well items will perform. Marketplaces decide on approval, and results depend on price and competition. A feed removes the preventable errors that stop products from being considered.

## What a well-built feed includes

- A clean product sheet with consistent titles, brands and units.
- Required fields mapped to each channel's field names.
- Variants grouped under a parent item, with sizes and colors set correctly.
- Barcodes, brand names and manufacturer part numbers checked.
- Rules that change titles, prices or categories for each channel.
- Filters that leave out products you do not want on a channel.
- Stock and price fields that refresh from your store.
- A schedule for updates that matches how often your data changes.
- A test upload with the errors cleared.
- A written map of which source field feeds which channel field.

## How we build it

We begin with an export of your catalog and look for gaps and patterns. We agree the rules with you, then map the fields for the first channel and build the feed. A test upload through the marketplace's checker shows what it dislikes, and we fix each error until the report is clean.

The Basic package covers one marketplace feed from your product sheet. Standard connects the feed to your store and adds rules for titles, prices, categories, variants and identifiers. Premium covers feeds for several channels from a single source, with filters, barcode and brand checks, a schedule and a guide for your team. If a feed app is used, you pay its maker directly.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Keep one master catalog and treat it as the source of truth.
- Use real barcodes from the manufacturer where they exist.
- Write titles that name the product plainly.
- Check the feed again after any big change to your store.
- Keep image links pointed at stable files.

**Avoid:**
- Editing products directly in the channel when a feed controls them.
- Inventing barcodes to pass a check.
- Using promotional text in the title field.
- Sending products the channel does not allow.
- Leaving the feed errors report unread.

## Who it is for

A store owner with several hundred products whose upload keeps failing. A seller adding Google Shopping or a marketplace who wants products to appear correctly on day one. A business that changes prices and stock often and needs updates to flow without manual uploads.

## What we need from you

Send a product export or give collaborator or staff access to your store, and name the channels you want to feed. Tell us about any products to exclude. We never need passwords. You enter any channel account details yourself, or add us as a limited user.
